$doc: Vyomi capability registry — Azure API Management. See aws/s3.json for the contract.

azure.apim.service.crud.title: API Management services (create, get, list, delete) over ARM

azure.apim.service.protocols.title: Protocol settings / Protocols + ciphers (properties.customProperties)
limitations: ENFORCED against the service's own "Test connection" action (apis/{id}/testConnect): a client connecting with a legacy protocol (TLS 1.0/1.1, SSL 3.0) this service has disabled is rejected exactly as the real gateway would refuse the handshake; TLS 1.2+ is always accepted (not independently toggle-able). Vyomi has no real TLS stack, so this is checked at the console's Test action rather than during an actual TLS negotiation, and cipher suite selection itself is still not modeled.

azure.apim.apis.crud.title: APIs (create, get, list, delete) — a real ARM sub-resource of the service

azure.apim.apis.createflows.title: Creating an API from WebSocket, GraphQL, gRPC, OpenAPI, WSDL, WADL, or an Azure resource (API App / Function App / Container App / Logic App); restricting a new API to specific gateways
limitations: HTTP, WebSocket, GraphQL and gRPC are modeled (display name, name, backend URL, API URL suffix, description, product — properties.apiType round-trips through ARM exactly like real APIM). Importing from a definition file (OpenAPI/WSDL/WADL) or an Azure resource (API App/Function App/Container App/Logic App), and per-API gateway restriction, are not simulated — new APIs are always reachable on the managed gateway.

azure.apim.products.crud.title: Products (create, get, list, delete) and product↔API association — real ARM sub-resources of the service
limitations: The "Visibility" column (developer-portal group association) is not modeled; products always show no visibility groups.

azure.apim.subscriptions.crud.title: Subscriptions (create, get, list, delete) — a real ARM sub-resource of the service
limitations: Primary/secondary keys are simulator-generated tokens, not real signing keys; the Owner column is not modeled (no AAD identity is attached to a subscription).

azure.apim.namedvalues.crud.title: Named values, Plain and Secret (create, get, list, delete) — a real ARM sub-resource of the service

azure.apim.namedvalues.keyvaultref.title: Named values of type Key Vault
limitations: The secret identifier only resolves against a Key Vault secret created in this SAME Vyomi space (the simulator's one Key Vault secrets store) — it can't reach an external vault, same as every other cross-service reference in Vyomi.

azure.apim.backends.crud.title: Backends (create, get, list, delete) — a real ARM sub-resource of the service

azure.apim.locks.title: Resource locks (Microsoft.Authorization/locks), scoped to the service
limitations: Lock create/list/delete are real Microsoft.Authorization/locks over ARM at resource, resource-group and subscription scope (CanNotDelete/ReadOnly, name and notes validated); this blade manages the locks scoped to this API Management service only and has no scope switch. A resource-group or subscription lock really blocks writes and deletes of everything under it with 409 ScopeLocked (core/azure_arm_ext_core.py lock_conflict), but a lock set directly on a API Management service is stored and listed only: it does not block writes or deletes of the API Management service itself.

azure.apim.activity_log.title: Activity log
limitations: Only console/SDK-triggered mutations made since the simulation booted are recorded (no historical backfill); severity/category filtering is not modeled, and `caller` is a fixed placeholder identity rather than the real signed-in principal. The timespan picker IS enforced — it maps to a real `eventTimestamp ge/le` $filter.

azure.apim.iam.title: Access control (IAM) on a service: role assignments and built-in role definitions over ARM
limitations: Role assignments and role definitions are real ARM resources (Microsoft.Authorization/roleAssignments, roleDefinitions). The Role assignments list IS scoped to this one service (plus its subscription/resource-group ancestors, matching real inherited access) — but 'Check access' / 'My access' evaluation, Deny assignments and Classic administrators are not modeled, and Vyomi never denies a console action based on a role assignment. Update: the Deny assignments list, Classic administrators (a read-only list of the subscription's account administrator, like the real API) and My access (the simulated signed-in principal, evaluated with checkAccess) are now real shared tabs (azure.common.*); the gap wording above predates them.

azure.apim.developerportal.title: Developer portal (overview, settings, Users, Groups, Identities, Delegation)
limitations: Users, Groups and Identity providers are real ARM sub-resources (service/users, service/groups, service/identityProviders) — create/list/delete round-trip exactly like Products or Backends. Delegation is a real portalsettings/delegation singleton (URL + validation key + the two delegate switches).

The developer portal CMS itself (its pages, theming, the live preview) and sign-in/sign-up self-service (registering as the portal's own visitor) are not modeled — there is no rendered portal site in Vyomi, only the ARM-level directory and settings that would drive one.

azure.apim.diagnosticsettings.title: Diagnostic settings (Microsoft.Insights/diagnosticSettings, scoped to this service)
limitations: Logs/metrics are never actually delivered to the configured destination (workspace, storage account or event hub) — there is no agent/telemetry pipeline, so the setting is stored and validated exactly as the real resource requires but nothing flows.

Vyomi has no catalog of APIM's real log/metric category names (GET .../diagnosticSettingsCategories is not modeled) — the create form offers the 'allLogs' category group and 'AllMetrics' rather than APIM's specific category picker.

azure.apim.monitoring.appinsights.title: Application Insights (the logger that links an Application Insights/Event Hub target)
limitations: The logger link (Microsoft.ApiManagement/service/loggers) is a real ARM sub-resource — create, list, delete round-trip exactly like Backends. Vyomi never actually emits request telemetry to the linked Application Insights resource or Event Hub (same gap as Diagnostic settings: azure.apim.diagnosticsettings).

azure.apim.monitoring.alerts.title: Alerts (metric alert rules scoped to this service)
limitations: Alert rules are real Microsoft.Insights/metricAlerts resources scoped (properties.scopes) to this service — create/list/delete round-trip through ARM like any other alert rule (azure.monitor.alert_rules). They never actually fire: Vyomi has no APIM request/latency metric time-series for a rule to evaluate against.

azure.apim.monitoring.title: Metrics, Logs, Analytics
limitations: Metrics and Logs are real dashboards over this service's stored data (API/product/subscription counts, the real Activity log's management-plane writes). Analytics now ALSO reports real gateway traffic: request counts, status classes, per API/operation/subscription and latency, computed from requests that actually went through the simulated gateway (azure.apim.gateway). An Azure Monitor metric time-series (Requests/Duration/Capacity charts via Microsoft.Insights) is not emitted, and 'Monitor + secure' on the create wizard (wiring a NEW service to Log Analytics / Application Insights / Defender for APIs) is still not modeled.

azure.apim.scaletier.title: Scale out and up, Pricing tier (post-creation sku.name/sku.capacity over ARM)
limitations: The Consumption (no scale units) and Developer (capped at exactly 1 unit) capacity limits ARE enforced on every PUT/PATCH. Other tiers' maximum unit counts and multi-region/zone scale-out are not — the tier name and unit count you set are stored and reflected in Overview and every other blade exactly as configured.

azure.apim.defender.title: Microsoft Defender for Cloud (this API Management service's recommendations)
limitations: Shows the live Defender for Cloud recommendations for this resource from Vyomi's rule engine (see azure.defender.recommendations); Azure's full built-in recommendation catalogue is not reproduced.

azure.apim.deployment.title: Network, Custom domains, Locations, Managed identities (user-assigned), Certificates, Gateways, Self-hosted gateways
limitations: Network (virtualNetworkType), Custom domains (hostnameConfigurations) and Locations (additionalLocations) are real properties.* fields on the service, written through the same PATCH the create wizard uses — ENFORCED for Locations: the Consumption and Developer tiers cannot add a region, same as real APIM (azure.apim.scaletier). 'Gateways' shows the resulting managed-gateway regions (primary + additional locations) read back from that same real data.
Certificates and Self-hosted gateways are real ARM sub-resources (service/certificates, service/gateways) — create/list/delete round-trip exactly like Backends.

User-assigned managed identities are real (see azure.apim.service.identity). Actual VNet connectivity, custom-domain TLS termination, and a self-hosted gateway's real connection back to the cloud service are not simulated — only their ARM-level configuration is.

azure.apim.apitags.crud.title: API Tags (Microsoft.ApiManagement/service/tags) — create, get, list, delete
limitations: Associating a tag with a specific API (apiTagResources) is not modeled; this page manages the service-wide tag catalog only, same as named values/backends.

azure.apim.policyfragments.crud.title: Policy fragments (Microsoft.ApiManagement/service/policyFragments) — create, get, list, delete
limitations: Vyomi stores the fragment's XML exactly as configured but never evaluates or injects it into a live request pipeline — Vyomi's gateway does not execute policies.

azure.apim.workspaces.title: Workspaces
limitations: Workspaces are a real ARM sub-resource (service/workspaces) — create/list/delete round-trip exactly like Products. Per-workspace delegated RBAC and a workspace's own scoped APIs/products/subscriptions sub-tree are not modeled; a workspace here is a flat named record.

azure.apim.credentialmanager.title: Credential manager (authorization providers)
limitations: Authorization providers are a real ARM sub-resource (service/authorizationProviders) — create/list/delete round-trip exactly like Backends. The nested per-provider Authorizations (the actual OAuth2 token exchange with the third-party identity provider) and the "Login" consent flow are not modeled — there is no third party to authorize against.

azure.apim.mcpservers.title: MCP Servers
limitations: An MCP server is modeled as a real API (service/apis) with apiType "mcp" — it is created, listed and deleted through the exact same ARM sub-resource as any other API (azure.apim.apis.crud), just filtered to that type. The actual Model Context Protocol surface (tool discovery, tool invocation over the gateway) is not implemented — Vyomi's gateway does not run an MCP server.

azure.apim.tools.title: Diagnose and solve problems, Support + Troubleshooting, Tasks
limitations: Diagnose and solve problems is real: detectors (core/azure_diagnose_core.py) are computed from the resource's live configuration, child resources and recorded operations; there is no platform telemetry behind a simulator, so none reads invented metrics and there is no AI troubleshooter.

Tasks are real Logic App workflows (Recurrence trigger plus Http-to-ARM actions, core/azure_tasks_core.py): scheduled runs call the simulator's own ARM and keep results in the run output; only Recurrence triggers and Http/Compose actions run, there is no e-mail or Teams connector, and Nano only fires schedules while the tab is open.

azure.apim.exporttemplate.title: Export template
limitations: All three tabs (ARM Template, Bicep, Terraform) are generated from the live resource's own known shape, not a general decompiler for arbitrary resources.

azure.apim.gateway_apis.title: API to self-hosted gateway association (service/gateways/{gw}/apis/{api})
limitations: service/gateways/{gw}/apis/{api} associations are ENFORCED by the gateway data plane: a request that selects a self-hosted gateway (header x-vyomi-apim-gateway: {gw}) is served only for APIs associated with it (others 404, unknown gateway 404); the managed gateway serves every API. There is no separate self-hosted gateway process to deploy; the gateway name is selected per request.

azure.apim.softdelete.title: Soft-delete: deleted services list, restore (properties.restore) and purge
limitations: Deleting a service keeps a 48-hour soft-deleted record (with its APIs, products and other children) under deletedservices; reusing the name conflicts until it is restored or purged. The record is not purged automatically when the date passes (purge is manual), and the restored service keeps its stored configuration only.

azure.apim.gateway.title: Gateway data plane: routing, subscription keys, policies, backends, request analytics and the Capacity gauge
limitations: Served at /azure-data/apim/{service}/{api-path}/{operation} (the real https://{service}.azure-api.net host is not bound). REAL: longest-prefix API routing + operation matching ({param} templates), Ocp-Apim-Subscription-Key / subscription-key (missing, invalid, suspended and out-of-scope keys give the real 401 messages; master, all-APIs, API- and product-scoped subscriptions), global/API/operation policy scopes composed through <base />, and the policies rate-limit, rate-limit-by-key, quota, quota-by-key, set-header, set-query-parameter, rewrite-uri, mock-response (operation sample), return-response, set-backend-service (base-url / backend-id), validate-jwt, check-header, set-body (literal) and cors (origins). Any other policy element is skipped and named in the x-vyomi-apim-skipped-policies response header (never silently passed); only a small @(...) expression subset is evaluated.

validate-jwt verifies HS256 signatures against issuer-signing-keys; RS256/ES256 tokens are claims-checked (exp/nbf/issuer/audience/required-claims) but the signature is NOT verified (response carries x-vyomi-apim-warning: jwt-signature-unverified). No response caching, schema validation, or WebSocket/gRPC/GraphQL pass-through.

The Capacity gauge and Analytics are computed from the real requests above against a nominal requests/second per SKU unit; the real gauge is CPU/memory-based, which a simulator does not have. Nano: policies, mock-response, return-response and all rejections work; forwarding to a backend returns 502 because a browser tab has no outbound sockets.

azure.apim.tasks.title: Tasks (Logic App-backed task templates)
limitations: A task is a REAL Microsoft.Logic/workflows record (Recurrence trigger + Http actions against management.azure.com) created from a template via POST .../Microsoft.Logic/vyomiCreateTask; runs are fired by the simulator scheduler (core/schedule_core.py) or 'Run now' and call the simulator's own ARM, so the effect is real (power state, restarts, key rotation, usage snapshots), with per-action results in Microsoft.Logic/workflows/runs. Only Recurrence triggers and Http-to-ARM/Compose actions run (anything else fails the run with ActionNotSupported); the managed identity is not authorised (RBAC is not evaluated); workflow expressions are not evaluated; there are no e-mail/Teams connectors, so report tasks keep their result in the run output. Missed schedules coalesce into one run; Nano only fires schedules while the tab is open.
